title: Speaker icon appears on applications that have the same name of the audio context name
line: The task manager no longer puts the speaker icon on an app just because another app's audio stream has the same name.
explanation: The task manager matches audio streams to tasks by process ID, and falls back to the stream's application name when an app never matched by PID. That fallback also took streams that already belonged to another running task, so e.g. Dolphin Emulator's "Dolphin" stream or an Electron app's "Chromium" stream also lit up Dolphin or Chromium. Streams matched to a task by PID are now marked and skipped by the name fallback.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: don't name-match audio streams of other tasks

A stream whose process belongs to a task was still matched by its
application name to other running tasks, so a Konsole child named Dolphin
put the audio indicator on Dolphin too. Such streams are now skipped.

BUG: 472539

media.caption: Konsole's child process plays a stream named "Dolphin": both Konsole and Dolphin show the speaker
Same setup with the fix: only Konsole shows the speaker

reviews.text: The fix cleanly prevents PID-matched audio streams from leaking into another task's app-name fallback, solving the native Konsole/Dolphin and native Electron/Chromium cases. However, streams matched via streamsForAppId(task.appId) for PipeWire portal / Flatpak apps are never marked as matched, so a Flatpak Dolphin Emulator or Flatpak Electron app (major real-world instances of this bug and duplicate 500045) will still put a bogus speaker icon on native Dolphin or Chromium.
changes: Mark streams matched via streamsForAppId(task.appId) as matched/claimed as well (e.g. rename pidMatched to a general matched flag and register matched streams for both appId and PID matches, emitting streamsChanged() when newly claimed) so portal/Flatpak streams are also skipped by streamsForAppName().
